content: Your doctor has prescribed famotidine to reduce the production of acid in your stomach. This medication is used to treat and prevent ulcers and to manage conditions where the stomach produces excessive acid. Famotidine will be administered either by adding it to an intravenous (IV) fluid that drips into a vein through a needle or catheter over at least 15 minutes, once or twice daily, or by continuous infusion over 24 hours. In some cases, famotidine may be prescribed for other purposes. If you have questions about its use, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Your healthcare provider may monitor the effectiveness of the treatment and check for side effects through laboratory tests and physical examinations. It is essential to attend all scheduled appointments with your doctor and the laboratory. The duration of your treatment will depend on how well you respond to the medication. Before starting famotidine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to famotidine, cimetidine (Tagamet), nizatidine (Axid), ranitidine (Zantac), or any other medications. Additionally, provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, including vitamins. Let your doctor know if you have a history of kidney or liver disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking famotidine, contact your doctor immediately. Before administering famotidine, inspect the solution carefully. It should appear clear and free of any floating particles. Do not use the solution if it is discolored, contains particles, or if the bag or container is leaking. Instead, use a new solution and show the damaged one to your healthcare provider. Follow the dosing instructions exactly as directed by your healthcare provider. Do not alter your dosing schedule without consulting them. If you encounter a mechanical issue, such as a blockage in the tubing, needle, or catheter, your healthcare provider may advise you to stop the infusion. If this happens, contact your healthcare provider immediately to resume therapy. Famotidine may cause side effects. Notify your healthcare provider if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: Headache Dizziness Constipation Diarrhea If you are receiving famotidine intravenously, your healthcare provider will likely supply you with several days' worth of medication at a time. You will probably be instructed to store the medication in the refrigerator or freezer. Take the next dose out of the refrigerator one hour before use and place it in a clean, dry area to allow it to reach room temperature. If you are storing additional doses in the freezer, transfer a 24-hour supply to the refrigerator each day for the following day’s use. Do not refreeze the medication. Keep all supplies in a clean, dry place and out of reach of children. Your healthcare provider will explain how to safely dispose of used needles, syringes, tubing, and containers to prevent accidental injury. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. If you are receiving famotidine through an IV or under the skin, be aware of the signs of a catheter-related infection. Contact your healthcare provider immediately if you notice any of the following symptoms near the catheter site: Tenderness Warmth Irritation Drainage Redness Swelling Pain Famotidine is available under the brand names Pepcid I.V. and Pepcid Premixed in Iso-osmotic Sodium Chloride Injection.
